assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:fido@original-light-novels#86-fido-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-6 Fido character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, with V10's first-person Fido chapter as the direct interior source and twelve audited Alter.1 ordinary-life controls; Alter.2 is excluded. The profile's Appendix A prints all 293 diagnostic rows (86-CMR-FID-001 to 293) with an exact route and Japanese anchor; 12 carry a frozen Phase-5 locator and 281 are LOCATOR_GAP rows. The governing method, CMR-9 audit and ledger, ledgers L01, L02 and L09, Documents 08, 09 and 12, other characters' profiles, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15 onward or Alter.2 scene is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Fido from his prewar origin as Prototype 008 in the Nouzen household, as V10 recounts it, through V14, with audited Alter.1 ordinary life unplaced in the volume chronology. States split at the located knowledge change: before the Federacy reactivation he believes the adolescent Shin a substitute for the child; at reactivation he hears 'シンエイ' and recognizes them as the same person (V10 p-030 ¶250-255, FID-234 to FID-237), then asks to serve again. V10 discloses to the reader an interior that predates the series; it does not mark a personality change. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: his origin, the naming and the family's removal belong to him at every later state, while earlier focalizers do not share V10's disclosures.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a discriminating account of Fido, the artificial-intelligence Scavenger attached to Shin (Shinei Nouzen): an analytical priority order (human nonharm and the creator's 'good friend to humans' wish, called 存在理由 and 絶対 at FID-165 and FID-199; protecting and accompanying particular humans, above all Shin; assigned support functions; local movement and standby orders), intervention-threshold conditions (Shin in immediate danger, an extraction or supply need, a memorial object to save, exclusion that looks unnecessary), and a conditional valuation of his own continuation (he preserved himself while he had people to search for and a master to serve, and narrates no reason to spare himself once he would lose a master again, FID-193 to FID-197). V10's first-person chapter supplies the deciding reasons for his central choices: choosing Shin knowing the attachment is 代償行為 and because this Shin is kind (FID-179, FID-180), and classing the Legion outside the friendship rule (FID-201, FID-202). It predicts mistakes and overreach: lower-order disobedience, self-condemnation that judges what end he deserves (FID-172), a morally asymmetric classification, and complicity in Frederica's smuggling. Not A: the priority order is an inference, not a source listing; interior access is concentrated in one V10 chapter; postwar purpose, directive revision and copy identity are open. Not C: the evidence says what changes his response and why, in his own narration where it matters most, and states where the account stops.

The profile's developmental model locates each state with its body, knowledge and relations: prewar Prototype 008 in the Nouzen household and the naming by child Shin; the family's removal under standby and the nonharm rule; transfer of his full configuration into a Scavenger body; years of searching while units die; choosing the adolescent Shin while believing him a substitute; the second naming; V01 learned memorial work; the V02 rebuilding around the surviving core; V03-V06 escalating intervention; V07 Shin's refusal to make him a weapon; V08 claimed leisure inclusion; V10 as disclosure to the reader rather than a change of personality; V11-V14 ordinary membership and the V14 rescue initiative (FID-274). The key knowledge change is located: at reactivation in the Federacy he hears 'シンエイ' and recognizes that the adolescent and the child are the same person (FID-234 to FID-237), then asks to serve again (FID-243, FID-244). Not A: V11-V14 are given as behavior clusters rather than a volume-by-volume state sequence, and V09 and V13 carry no located state of their own. Not C: each state carries its own constraints and evidence, and personality change is separated from reader disclosure.

Two layers are specified and kept apart. The interior first-person narration, attested in the V10 chapter, uses わたくし with humble and service morphology (僭越ながら, お仕えする, 嬉しゅうございます, 光栄でございます, 面目次第もございません, お許しいただけますか) and a per-person address system (旦那様 or 我が創造主, 奥様, 兄君, 弟君, ノウゼン様 becoming 我が主 and, after recognition, わたくしの最初で最後の主, シュガ様, リッカ様, ククミラ様, エマ様). Emotion shortens and repeats units without becoming colloquial (いいえ。いいえ; 寂しく、哀しい), and technical vocabulary coexists with affect. The external layer has no speech output (FID-154): beeps, sensor blinking, posture, crane-arm gestures and action, with Shin a special decoder (FID-187) and no general lexicon; the V10 reactivation scene shows both layers at once (「ぴ……」 beside 面目次第もございません, FID-241 and FID-242). Not A: the interior register comes from one chapter in one narrative mode, and the external layer cannot be translated into sentences. Not C: the register is located across joy, grief, guilt, technical self-description and farewell and across addressees, with explicit negative constraints.

Ordinary conduct recurs across volumes with stated conditions: dancing to make a lonely Shin laugh (FID-118), target games and harder can formations, setting fireworks, fishing after ignoring a wait order (FID-106), approaching sea animals (FID-260 to FID-262), the failed fruit-cutting game, camp logistics, collecting trash, bringing a drum can, serving as a windbreak and bench, Alter.1's group nap against him (FID-285 to FID-290) and out-of-season lilac branches as a gift (FID-292). The predictive model covers a familiar group starting leisure (approach or join when the body allows) and bodily failure (visible dejection, then continued presence). Not A: Alter.1 is supplemental, and the exact affect behind each movement is a human gloss. Not C: the behaviors are conditioned on feasibility, familiarity and exclusion, not merely listed.

Twelve directed relation models condition his conduct: child Shin as foundational (naming, learning through him); Vaclav Nouzen as creator whose wish he internalizes; Maika and Rei remembered distinctly; adolescent and current Shin in layers (initial choice under a mistaken identity model, dyadic decoding, stubbornness, escalating protection, Shin's refusal to instrumentalize him, re-choice after recognition); Raiden, whose fatalism he rejects at his apparent death (FID-214, FID-215); Theo, Kurena and Anju addressed individually at the same boundary (FID-207 to FID-213); Frederica, with practical familiarity and shared boundary testing under a comic sanction (FID-255 to FID-257); Lena, Rito and Marcel, base personnel, the Legion and unfamiliar animals. Not A: the profile marks Lena, Maika and Rei, and Theo, Kurena and Anju beyond the farewell as thin, and it forbids inferring reverse symmetry from his devotion. Not C: the Shin layers, Raiden, Frederica and the Legion are distinctly conditioned with located controls.

The V10 chapter gives direct first-person interiority on his decisive choices: replaying the family's removal and asking why he did nothing (FID-161 to FID-169); emptiness after concluding the family dead and judging destruction a fitting end (FID-172); choosing Shin while naming the attachment as compensatory (FID-179, FID-180); feeling that Shin understands him (FID-187); reasons for self-sacrifice and the Legion classification; honour at receiving the plates (FID-220 to FID-223); farewell, the vision of the dead and the plea to be forgiven (FID-225 to FID-230); recognition and re-choice (FID-234 to FID-249). The profile separates this from external behavior and from human glosses. Not A: interior access is confined to the V10 retrospective chapter; other volumes give only behavior and focalizers' interpretations. Not C: the interior states the deciding reasons in his own narration rather than leaving them to inference.

Opposition is conditioned by stakes and feasibility: lower-order wait and standby orders lose to remaining near or helping people he values (standing watch after a standby order, FID-043, FID-044; boarding transports; fishing against a wait order); exclusion produces insistent following and 'tantrum'-like persistence, with the label treated as a gloss and the persistence as fact; a sanction threatening his deployment with Shin draws a vivid reaction; an instruction that requires harming a human is refused with very high confidence; under acute rescue urgency he rams, shields or carries before signalling. Not A: the profile rates the stable-tendency form of his disobedience moderate and says the exact behavior depends on feasibility and stakes; verbal argument is unavailable to him. Not C: the hierarchy and threshold conditions explain which side wins in the located conflicts.

His own reasoning is narrated at located choices: whether something else could have been done when the nonharm rule and standby state bound him, producing the decision to search; whether to keep preserving himself, answered by the loss of his reason to; whether the Legion are beings his friendship rule protects (FID-199 to FID-203, concluding they are not); whether to serve again after recognition, asked as permission. The profile identifies moral risk in the Legion classification and refuses to generalize it. Not A: artificial-to-artificial ethics beyond the Legion case, memory and copy consent and civic standing are open, and the deliberation is retrospective in one chapter. Not C: the reasoning is his own and the priority order explains the outcomes.

Humor is located with its source and limits: embodiment comedy (a ten-ton dance, the lunge into wreckage at the V02 reunion, impossible fruit handling, sulking), play aimed at others' pleasure (dancing to make Shin laugh, harder target formations), the exuberant dance at the second naming by the adolescent Shin (FID-121 to FID-124), and the V14 wish to mount a recovered gun, drooping when reminded he lacks balance and fire control and brightening at the fireworks alternative (FID-277 to FID-280). The emotional-state deltas say when play stops: acute rescue urgency turns expressive signalling into body-first action. Not A: his own view of play is little narrated beyond the naming, and the comic emotional labels are human glosses. Not C: function, audience and the switch to urgency are conditioned.

One canonical derived profile (about 134 KB) covers V01-V14 and audited Alter.1 with 293 diagnostic controls, each with an exact EPUB route and Japanese anchor; 12 reuse frozen Phase-5 locators and 281 are LOCATOR_GAP rows. Not B: it is a single derived surface subordinate to ledgers, Documents 08, 09 and 12 and source verification that are not curated on this subject; most controls lack frozen locators; V15 onward, Alter.2 and the anime are excluded. Not D: coverage spans the whole locked corpus with exact routes and separates three evidence modes.

Affirmative limits are located: no ordinary speech output (FID-154); no combat fire-control, and a recovered heavy gun would destabilize him (FID-277 to FID-280); manipulators poor for delicate tasks; weight and terrain limits; the friendship and nonharm directive described as unbreakable and 絶対, so a reconstruction cannot make him discard it; direct narration that losing the chance to accompany others is lonely and sad, so he is not fearless; focalizers' glosses such as Annette's 'worried' reading (FID-087, FID-088) do not become exact; ordinary Scavengers as a negative control; the Legion classification is not a general theory of artificial persons. Not A: some limits rest on single scenes. Not C: these are located affirmative evidence, not silence.

States are located by period, body and knowledge: before the recognition at the Federacy reactivation he believes the adolescent Shin a substitute; after it he knows they are the same person and addresses him as his first and last master. V10 is treated as disclosure to the reader, not a change of chronology or personality, and Alter.1 is audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence. Not A: V11-V14 states are clustered rather than sequenced, and Alter.1 scenes are not placed in a volume chronology. Not C: the decisive knowledge change is located at FID-234 to FID-237, and the profile forbids projecting V10 knowledge onto earlier focalizers.

conditions: Interior first-person narration only, in written Japanese, illustrative and never presented as quotation: わたくし with humble and service morphology and the located per-person address terms, chosen by state (ノウゼン様 before recognition, わたくしの最初で最後の主 after it).

External interaction is rendered as beeps, sensor blinking, posture, crane-arm gesture and action, never as spoken sentences or a translated beep lexicon, unless a new communication technology is explicitly introduced.
Human interpretations of his signals are labelled as interpretations; Shin's understanding is dyadic, not a general decoder.
Strong emotion shortens and repeats formal units; it does not turn colloquial.
scenario_readiness.note: The interior register and the signal layer are specified separately; any generated text is noncanonical and bounded by these conditions.

conditions: Apply the priority order: nonharm to humans is absolute; protecting particular humans outranks assigned functions, which outrank local orders.
Fix his body: heavy and relatively slow, manipulators and containers, no speech output, no fire control.
Exclude copy or backup identity, memory ownership or consent, legal standing, revision of the directive and a postwar vocation.
Transfer to an unsampled relationship is a separate, lower-confidence condition; generalized care for unfamiliar humans is moderate confidence.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A located state: the search years; Spearhead and Special Recon service while he believes the adolescent Shin a substitute; after the Federacy rebuilding and the recognition at reactivation (FID-234 to FID-249); or V11-V14 ordinary membership. No V15 onward, Alter.2 or postwar state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Shin (primary), Raiden, Theo, Kurena and Anju at the depth the profile gives, Frederica, base personnel; Lena, Rito and Marcel at lower depth; unfamiliar humans and animals under the moderate rule; Legion as the hostile classification.
setting_constraints: Military support, camp, leisure, memorial or rescue situations matched to the located cases.
No new communication technology, combat vocation or armed conversion.
No copy or backup, memory-consent, civic-standing or directive-revision scenario.

scenario_readiness.note: The priority order, threshold conditions, body limits and relation models support bounded novel situations. Not READY: interior access is confined to one chapter and several open questions block whole scenario classes. Not NOT_READY: matched support, leisure, exclusion and rescue cases are explained.

conditions: Settings sampled: group leisure and games, camp logistics, quiet co-presence with Shin, group rest against his body, gift-bringing.
Participation depends on bodily feasibility; failure brings visible dejection and continued presence, not withdrawal.
Render his part through action and signals, not speech.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary group life is well sampled; the exact affect behind each movement is a gloss.

conditions: Matched dilemmas only: human nonharm against an instruction, protection against self-preservation, local orders against remaining with or helping people he values, classification of a hostile machine.
Keep the nonharm and friendship directive absolute; do not stage its rejection as liberation.
No artificial-peer ethics beyond the Legion case, memory or copy consent, or civic-rights reasoning.
scenario_readiness.note: His own reasoning is narrated at the located choices, and the priority order explains their outcomes.
The curated profile does not address romantic relationships.

conditions: Scavenger support and recovery work: resupply under fire, salvage, towing, transport, memento recovery, camp logistics and rescue.
Respect the mechanical limits: no fire control, weight, terrain and manipulator limits.
Not supported: a combat vocation, command, rank, pay or institutional rights.
scenario_readiness.note: His support role is densely sampled; institutional status and a combat role are not.

known_limits.statement: He has no ordinary speech output; external communication is beeps, sensors, posture, gesture and action, with no general lexicon.
The creator's 'good friend to humans' wish and the human-nonharm rule are his 存在理由 and 絶対; the corpus never shows him rejecting them.
His violent acts are rescue interventions; he lacks fire control and a heavy gun would destabilize him.
Human readings of his movements (worried, sulking, proud) are focalizers' interpretations; V10 establishes that he has emotions, not that each gloss is exact.
Direct interior access comes from the V10 first-person chapter; other volumes give behavior and human interpretation only.
His classification of the Legion as outside the friendship rule is not a general theory of artificial persons.
The only curated item is a derived profile subordinate to narrower authorities; 281 of its 293 controls are LOCATOR_GAP rows with exact routes but no frozen locator.
Lena, Maika and Rei, and Theo, Kurena and Anju beyond the farewell are less specified than his Spearhead and Shin relations.
Copy or backup identity, memory ownership and consent, civic standing, revision of the directive and a postwar vocation are open.
The curated profile does not address romance.
